studies.study: Desmurget et al., Movement intention after parietal cortex stimulation
studies.finding: Parietal stimulation can evoke reported intention or perceived motion without detected target EMG; premotor stimulation can evoke overt movement with denial.
studies.relevance: Reported authorship/intent not reducible to movement
studies.limit: No complete physical signature; small clinical sample; intention not same as felt attempting.

studies.study: Kilteni et al., Motor imagery involves predicting sensory consequences
studies.finding: Imagined self-touch attenuates felt real touch with spatiotemporal constraints
studies.relevance: Efference/sensory prediction can be recruited without overt executed movement
studies.limit: Does not establish same phenomenal agency during imagery and action.

studies.study: Han et al., Sensory attenuation in the absence of movement
studies.n: two experiments; exact Ns not fully checked
studies.measure: EEG N1/Tb/P2 response to tones contingent on active choice vs passive
studies.finding: Active vs passive differed in Tb suppression and P2 enhancement even in conditions permitting sound without button movement; N1 did not differ
studies.relevance: Motor act, consequence control, and sensory signatures must be separated
studies.limit: No direct identity of ERP with named phenomenal quale; study-level condition confounds remain.

studies.study: Veillette, Lopes & Nusbaum, Temporal dynamics of brain activity predicting sense of agency
studies.measure: electrically driven movement, trial-wise explicit SoA judgement, EEG
studies.finding: Subjects sometimes attributed electrically actuated movement to self; early EEG predictor reported ~83ms and late patterns, peak cross-person classifier AUC 0.587
studies.relevance: Actual peripheral cause need not equal attributed cause; early and later signals are different
studies.limit: EEG prediction not causal demonstration; modest AUC; no complete phenomenal/physical organization.

studies.study: Pryke, Jayachandran & Martin, causal neural substrates of prospective and retrospective SoA
studies.measure: within-person tDCS/sham, free vs instructed key choice, reward vs punishment, action vs outcome intentional binding
studies.finding: Published reported valence main effect F(1,100)=44.49 p<.001; free-versus-instructed choice F=2.46 p=.120; site by stimulation F=4.24 p=.042
studies.relevance: Outcome valuation and neural perturbation modulate implicit binding; free choice is not sufficient marker
studies.limit: Free vs forced means free choice vs instructed key, NOT externally forced muscle motion; non-significance is not evidence of equality; temporal binding is not all agency; OSF raw not yet downloaded.

studies.study: Veillette, Cheng, Joshi & Nusbaum, binding and masked outcomes
studies.measure: reported temporal binding under visible versus masked action consequence
studies.finding: Binding abolished and apparently reversed for outcomes masked from awareness under studied protocol
studies.relevance: Outcome-access regime changes selected temporal agency indicator
studies.limit: Does not imply basal experience ceases; this is selected task/measure gate, not universal experience gate.

studies.study: Jurchiş, Preda, Costea & Skora, non-conscious regularities and instrumental conditioning
studies.measure: instrumental choices, trial-wise structural awareness and conscious judgment scales
studies.finding: Unaware-of-grammar structure can guide adaptive choices when judgment of predictive value is conscious; no robust completely-unaware judgment success
studies.relevance: Structural knowledge awareness, judgment awareness, adaptive intelligence differ
studies.limit: Unconscious structural information does NOT imply absence of basal phenomenal experience; consciousness measures are task report.

studies.study: Schneider, Nelson & Mooney, synaptic circuit basis for corollary discharge
studies.measure: intracellular recordings, optogenetic gain/loss of function
studies.finding: M2 to auditory cortex drive is causally implicated in movement-related auditory suppression
studies.relevance: Source-specific physical involvement in sensory processing without human verbal self-report

studies.study: Schneider, Sundararajan & Mooney, learned cortical filter
studies.n: multiple mouse experiments; condition-specific Ns in full text
studies.finding: Learning action-contingent sound selectively suppresses predicted auditory response and improves detection of novel tones during movement
studies.limit: Neural perceptual mechanisms, not report of felt doing; no ontic bridge test.

studies.study: Local and system mechanisms for action execution and observation
studies.measure: single-unit recordings, own grasping Go/NoGo vs observing human execution
studies.finding: Shared action observation regions but task- and area-specific firing dynamics, including both facilitated and suppressed cells
studies.relevance: Shared represented goal/object need not fix source/route/time organization
studies.limit: Action blocks not perfectly matched physical state; no first-person subject report; raw data on request only.

studies.study: Attenuation of responses to self-generated sounds in auditory cortical neurons
studies.measure: same physical sound animal-triggered vs random
studies.finding: Self-generated sound evokes attenuated mouse auditory responses in controlled trials, beyond general movement state effects
studies.relevance: Closer same-stimulus source/contingency contrast at neuron level
studies.limit: Verify exact DOI before formal manuscript citation; no direct mouse phenomenal report.
